description: What is the macro backdrop doing? Daily Macro Regime snapshot from 18 components in 6 tiers (Liquidity 30%, Financial Conditions 20%, Risk Appetite 15%, Crypto Liquidity 10%, Business Cycle 15%, Inflation/Real Rates 10%). FRED-sourced. Returns composite_score (0-100), regime_label (risk_off/neutral/risk_on_leaning/risk_on), cycle_phase_label (contraction/early_expansion/mid_expansion/late_expansion), matrix_quadrant (sweet_spot/late_cycle_warning/crisis/recovery), tier_scores (6 sub-scores), components (flat key/value of all 18), stale_components_detail and provenance. Four component keys mean something narrower than their name (vix_score, broad_dollar_index, fed_funds_rate, global_m2_yoy): component_notes in the payload defines each — read it before quoting one. A vix_score of 71 means VIX around 18.6; broad_dollar_index readings near 120 are normal. provenance is null for rows written before 2026-10-13, when coverage was not recorded; missing components drop out and the tier renormalizes, a tier with no input at all scores a stand-in 50 and is named in `degraded.empty_tiers`. Pass fields="full" for the named missing components, sources and per-tier provenance. `move_index` and `fed_funds_cuts_priced` are always null and never weighted — slots without a source, not outages. [Free tier]

fields.description: Omit for the default response, which carries `provenance` in short form (grade full/partial/thin, sources_used, sources_expected). 'full' adds the long form: sources_missing (named), sources (licence attribution names), grade_reason, as_of — plus per-part provenance where the composite has parts. A `thin` grade (under half the expected inputs) is never a basis for a verdict or a ranking.
